category_title: Students with learning disabilities who equate high-volume note-taking with learning and use abbreviations to increase speed
student_description: Ben is a conscientious student who equates high-volume note-taking with learning, leading him to struggle with keeping up during fast-paced lectures. He uniquely needs strategies that allow him to maintain his high output (like abbreviations) while providing structure (categorized notes, pre-quizzes) to guide his attention and manage cognitive load.

criteria.rationale: Providing specific categories helps Ben channel his high-volume writing into a manageable format that boosts his self-concept.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or prompts the use of a structured format with specific categories (e.g., Topic, Main Points, Vocabulary) for capturing notes during the lecture.

criteria.rationale: Priming Ben before the lecture helps him identify gaps in his prior knowledge and guides his attention during fast-paced content.
criteria.check: The tutor uses a pre-assessment, quiz, or targeted preview activity before the lecture begins to highlight what information Ben should look for.
